Alice / Soojin / Lauren,

Thanks — I reviewed Riverside's redline and tracked changes into Redwood's response (attached). Highlights / rationale:

1) Termination for convenience (Section 12):
   - Riverside requests a 90-day for-convenience termination. We are prepared to accept 90 days provided there is an explicit wind-down clause that:
     a) preserves any committed usage or prepaid credits paid by the customer for the remainder of the billing period, and
     b) allows Redwood to close out co-sell entitlements with Microsoft within the next settlement cycle (we propose language that requires notice of termination to be delivered to both Redwood and Microsoft's merchant account so settlement isn't disrupted).
   - Proposed compromise language is in the attached doc (see Sec 12(b)).

2) PO mapping & invoicing (Exhibit B):
   - We can accept a clause that obligates Redwood to reference the Riverside PO on invoices and to copy Riverside's billing contact. We cannot guarantee changes to Azure/MSFT merchant settlement mechanics; however, Redwood will provide an internal invoice reference that maps to the Azure merchant invoice id and the PO. This is an operational mapping, not affecting revenue share.

3) Co-sell revenue split and MSFT consent:
   - The co-sell split for this deal (as discussed) is 60/40 (Riverside/rev share to Redwood) in the commercial term sheet. Any material changes to how Azure settles will require coordination with Microsoft; Redwood will take ownership of those conversations but needs a 5-business-day window to notify Riverside before making changes to settlement ops.

4) Data processing note: added standard DPA reference and MSFT marketplace data flow notice (non-negotiable for marketplace listings).

If Riverside confirms the compromise on termination and accepts the PO-mapping operational note, we will finalize the redline and prepare the DocuSign packet.

Regards,
